knowledge-base.name: process-kill-safety
knowledge-base.triggers: pkill, killall, taskkill, Stop-Process, kill process, terminate process, stop process, kill by name
knowledge-base.overview: Hard rule: never run broad name-pattern process kills. Always use specific PIDs or explicit container names.

rule.statement: Broad name-pattern process kills are BANNED without explicit user permission.
rule.why: User has been burned by prior incidents where broad kills (e.g., `pkill node`, `Stop-Process -Name python`, `taskkill /IM chrome.exe`) terminated unrelated processes the user was relying on. The cost of one mis-kill is high (lost work, interrupted sessions); the cost of checking first is near zero.
rule.how-to-apply: Whenever you need to terminate a process, prefer the most specific targeting available.

alternative.use: kill PID | kill -9 PID | Stop-Process -Id PID | taskkill /PID pid | taskkill /F /PID pid

alternative.case: You have a named container or service
alternative.use: docker stop CONTAINER | docker-compose down SERVICE | systemctl stop UNIT | sc.exe stop SERVICE

alternative.case: You need to find the PID first
alternative.use: ps aux | grep NAME → copy PID → kill PID (two steps, intentional) | Get-Process NAME | Select Id → Stop-Process -Id PID | tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq NAME.exe" → taskkill /PID pid

alternative.case: You only have a name pattern and no PID is known
alternative.use: STOP. Ask the user before proceeding. Present the command you want to run and the reason.

knowledge-base.enforcement: A PreToolUse hook on Bash matches `pkill*`, `killall*`, `*Stop-Process*`, `*taskkill*/IM*` and injects a safety reminder before the command runs. If the hook fires, follow it: use a specific PID or ask the user.
knowledge-base.override: The user can explicitly grant permission in the current request ("go ahead and pkill all python processes — I don't have anything else running"). When they do, proceed. Otherwise the default is strict.
